name: Call for Aid
oracle_text: Gain control of all creatures target opponent controls until end of turn. Untap those creatures. They gain haste until end of turn. You can't attack that player this turn. You can't sacrifice those creatures this turn.
blocked_sentences: You can't sacrifice those creatures this turn.

needs.what: A spell/ability effect op that marks a set of permanents as unsacrificeable for the turn, so that any cost or effect that would sacrifice them (a `sacrifice` cost, the `sacrifice` op) cannot choose them -- the restriction that stops a borrowed creature being eaten before control reverts
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Nothing in `ops` or `static_effects` expresses a sacrifice prohibition; there is no `cant_be_sacrificed` anywhere in the engine. `lock_abilities` is the nearest relative -- it is an until-end-of-turn TempEffect that stops a permanent's activated abilities being activated -- but it gates the wrong thing: it cannot stop the `sacrifice` cost of an ability whose source is a *different* permanent (an Altar-style outlet), and it cannot stop the `sacrifice` op or any edict-style effect. `replace_deaths` redirects a permanent's death after the fact rather than making the sacrifice illegal, which is a different game action and lets the creature leave the battlefield anyway. `indestructible` via `grant_keyword` explicitly does not prevent sacrifice

resolved_note: `cant_attack_player` shipped: the op takes an `attacker` player spec, a `defender` player spec and a `duration` of `this_turn` or `this_combat`, recorded as a `structs.AttackRestriction` on `GameState.attack_restrictions` and read by the new `combat.attack_target_forbidden` seam. "You can't attack that player this turn" is `{"op": "cant_attack_player", "attacker": "you", "defender": {"target": "<the targeted opponent>"}, "duration": "this_turn"}`. Only `cant_sacrifice` is still missing; with it, and the existing `gain_control`, `untap` and `grant_keyword` (haste), the whole card loads. No partial answer was written because a Call for Aid that could not stop the borrowed creatures being sacrificed is a strictly better card than the printed one.
